articles.title: Home Assistant brings HACS into a built-in Marketplace
articles.dek: Community downloads move into Settings, with catalog installs that do not require a GitHub account.
body: Home Assistant brings HACS into a built-in Marketplace for community integrations, dashboard cards, themes and templates. Its Settings panel lets administrators browse, install and update catalog items without a GitHub account; custom repositories and alternative versions still use a GitHub connection.

Franck Nijhof carries existing HACS installations across automatically, preserving downloads, dashboard resources and custom repositories. Update notices join Home Assistant’s other updates, and existing HACS links keep working. AppDaemon apps and Python scripts stop being managed, with a repair notice identifying affected downloads.

The move keeps the risks of community code visible. Administrators must accept a trust warning before installation or updates, and replacing a built-in integration requires an additional confirmation. Community integrations still run inside Home Assistant, while custom cards run in users’ browsers.

articles.title: Music Assistant puts podcast transcripts beside the episode
articles.dek: Episode pages, readable transcripts and chapter lists give listeners more ways to follow a show.
body: Music Assistant gives podcast episodes their own page, with the full description, publication date, length, played status and nearby episodes. Listeners can read an available transcript or choose to play from that episode through to the latest one.

OzGav also brings timed transcripts into the full-screen player. When an inserted advertisement sends the text out of step, an unlink button freezes it; linking again adjusts the timing to resume where the programme continues. Manual timing adjustment remains available.

The interface builds on transcript support for Pocket Casts and feed-based podcast sources. It depends on a transcript being supplied; Pocket Casts’ own generated transcripts require its Plus or Patron plan. A companion correction finds external chapter files and loads chapters when an episode starts, without delaying playback.

articles.title: Music Assistant closes Home Assistant sign-ins for disabled accounts
articles.dek: Disabling an account blocks both Home Assistant entry points, while signing out closes connections using that login.
body: Music Assistant enforces an administrator’s decision to disable an account when someone signs in through Home Assistant or opens it from the sidebar. Those routes could previously create a replacement account, issue a token for the disabled one or fail with a database error.

Marcel van der Veldt also makes regular sign-in explain that an account is disabled after the correct password is supplied. Signing out through the HTTP interface closes app connections using that login token, and an unauthenticated sidebar connection receives no events until it authenticates.

articles.title: Sendspin’s C++ client adopts encrypted, paired connections
articles.dek: Device makers must adapt to new identities and pairing records as the audio client implements the release-candidate protocol.
body: Sendspin’s C++ client adopts the 1.0 release-candidate protocol with encrypted connections and pairing before a server can start playback. Applications can explicitly allow unpaired access, but that exception does not persist across a restart on its own.

Kevin Ahrendt’s implementation gives an upgraded device a new key-based identity and changes how applications store pairing records. Device makers must update their integration; an existing server will see a new client that needs pairing. The work was exercised on ESP32 hardware and against the updated Python server.
The client needs aiosendspin 10 on the server, which is still under development. Separate server corrections keep older Python and JavaScript clients able to pair during the transition.

Fix Pairing PSK on older aiosendspin and sendspin-js clients
Fix PIN pairing on older aiosendspin and sendspin-js clients
Fix PIN pairing on aiosendspin 7.x/8.x and sendspin-js 4.0.0

articles.title: iHeartRadio joins Music Assistant with radio and podcasts
articles.dek: Guest listening works without an account; signing in synchronizes followed stations, artists and podcasts.
body: Music Assistant adds iHeartRadio as a source for live radio, podcasts and artist-based stations in Australia, Canada, Mexico, New Zealand and the United States. People can listen as guests, browse stations by city or genre, and search for an artist to start a continuing mix.

Signing in connects followed stations, artists and podcasts to the library, with favourites reflected back to iHeartRadio. Setup chooses a country, with one connection per country. Album pages can list tracks but cannot play them on demand; that requires a paid tier the connection does not provide.

pullRequests.title: Add iHeartRadio provider

articles.title: Home Assistant saves Reolink images from before an event
articles.dek: An automation can retrieve a still from an existing recording instead of relying on a live snapshot.
body: Reolink owners gain a Home Assistant action for saving an image from an earlier recording. A person-detection automation could include a still from a minute before the detection, giving a notification context that a live snapshot would miss.

The camera must have a recording at the requested time. Reolink returns the nearest available key frame, so the image can be a few seconds away from the chosen instant; an event-only camera cannot supply a moment it did not record.

pullRequests.title: Add Reolink snapshot past action

articles.title: Home Assistant explores carrying server setup across Apple devices
articles.dek: An iCloud proposal would spare repeated URL entry while keeping each device’s registration separate.
body: Home Assistant is considering sharing server settings between iPhones, iPads and Macs signed into the same Apple Account. Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves proposes offering a known home on a new device instead of asking its owner to enter internal and external addresses again.

The first step would copy server configuration and still require the usual Home Assistant sign-in. Each device would register separately, keeping its own notifications, sensors and permissions. The proposal includes controls to disable syncing or exclude one server; sharing across different Apple Accounts and Android are outside its scope.

A later, opt-in phase would exchange a synced enrollment credential for a separate login session on each device. That would need new Core support and a security review, including access from shared Apple devices and how sessions are revoked. The proposal remains in Considering.

externalSources.title: (Apple) Sync companion app servers between same iCloud user devices

articles.title: ESPHome keeps Bluetooth proxies accepting new connections
articles.dek: Abandoned connection attempts no longer fill the radio’s hidden slots while the proxy reports them free.
body: ESPHome corrects a Bluetooth proxy failure where repeatedly abandoned connection attempts could leave the radio unable to connect to any device, even though the proxy reported free connection slots. Cancelling an attempt also cancels the pending operation in the Bluetooth stack.

Michael Heichler verified the correction on an Everything Presence Lite: the original firmware failed on the seventh aborted attempt, while the corrected version accepted a real device after runs of nine and 21 cancellations. This is his first contribution to ESPHome.

The cancellation needs ESP-IDF 5.5.5 or 6.0.1 and newer compatible framework versions; older versions keep the previous cancellation behavior. J. Nick Koston also guards against a stale queued connection that could crash an active Bluetooth device, applying that guard only to framework versions missing the upstream correction.

pullRequests.title: [bluetooth_connection] Cancel pending Bluedroid opens on disconnect
[esp32_ble_tracker] Guard Bluedroid against stale queued connection requests

articles.title: Home Assistant stops ViCare readings freezing the whole system
articles.dek: Heating readings are gathered in the background, avoiding freezes that trigger automatic restarts.
body: Home Assistant prevents ViCare heating readings from blocking the rest of the system. Since the 2026.9.0 coordinator change, reading a sensor could make a network request on the main processing loop and freeze it long enough for Supervisor to restart Home Assistant.

The integration gathers those values alongside its background update instead. The displayed readings then use the gathered results, avoiding a fresh network request as Home Assistant reads each sensor.

pullRequests.title: Read ViCare entity values in the executor

articles.title: Home Assistant OS fixes Raspberry Pi USB-storage lockups
articles.dek: Boot recovery avoids a restart loop, while Argon ONE M.2 systems get a storage workaround.
body: Home Assistant OS corrects two failures affecting Raspberry Pi systems using USB storage. One could leave a board in an endless restart loop after exhausting its normal boot attempts: the recovery information was saved just before a reboot cut power to the drive, losing the write.

Jan Čermák changes recovery to attempt a boot in the same pass. He also switches the Argon ONE M.2 case’s USB-to-SATA bridge to a different storage mode after reports of heavy writes freezing the system.

pullRequests.title: Refill boot tries before slot selection in U-Boot scripts
Disable UAS on RPi for Argon ONE M.2 (ASMedia 174c:1156)

articles.title: Music Assistant preserves speaker identities across restarts
articles.dek: Rooms, aliases and automations stay attached to the same speaker after a restart.
body: Music Assistant stops certain AirPlay, Chromecast or DLNA speakers acquiring a new identity after every restart. Home Assistant could consequently recreate the speaker’s entity and lose its assigned room, aliases and automations.

Marvin Schenkel corrects a stale stored link that let an unrelated native speaker claim an output it could not actually use. Genuine transfers of a speaker to its native connection retain their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: Fix a universal player getting a new id on every restart

articles.title: Music Assistant keeps lookups out of YouTube search history
articles.dek: Anonymous searches stop background library work appearing as searches made by the listener.
body: Music Assistant stops adding its YouTube Music searches to the listener’s YouTube search history. Background artist scans and lookups triggered by opening a library track had each created entries using the connected account.

Marvin Schenkel makes search anonymous again while other YouTube Music calls remain authenticated. The privacy change also lets unplayable or region-blocked tracks reappear in search results; filtering them is separate work.

pullRequests.title: Keep YouTube Music searches out of your YouTube search history

articles.title: Speech-to-Phrase gains Slovenian and Russian command grammar
articles.dek: Two languages gain the sentence sets needed to use their existing local speech models.
body: Speech-to-Phrase gains Slovenian and Russian command grammar, filling a gap that kept their existing acoustic models from serving those languages. Michael Hansen adapts community-written phrases into the bounded sentence sets used for local voice control.
Home Assistant’s broader command grammar is unchanged. Some requests, including lock-state questions and to-do items, remain outside these sentence sets.

pullRequests.title: Add Speech-to-Phrase sentences for Slovenian (sl) and Russian (ru)

articles.title: ESPHome removes a network hurdle from cached ESP32 builds
articles.dek: Cached components let firmware builds get past setup even when the component registry is unreachable.
body: ESPHome keeps local copies of the registry components required by its native ESP32 build system. Once those components are cached, configuring a firmware build no longer needs to reach the registry, so a poor connection or an offline host does not stop that step.

J. Nick Koston measured a stalled-network configuration step falling from 165 seconds to four. The local copies produce identical dependency selections and component files in tests against ESP-IDF 5.5.5 and 6.1.0. First downloads still need a connection, and components supplied through Git or local paths keep their existing behavior.

pullRequests.title: [espidf] Mirror registry components locally so configures skip the registry

roadmapUpdates.title: Automation target exclusions get a quieter design
roadmapUpdates.summary: Marcin Bauer shares a revised way to exclude individual automation targets, reducing extra dialogs and using subdued colours for a deliberate choice. Niels questions duplicated labels and suggests simplifying the grouping; the opportunity remains in Shaping.

sources.title: Let users exclude individual entities from resolved targets in automations/blueprints/scripts

roadmapUpdates.title: An app-replacement route does not fit the iOS transfer
roadmapUpdates.summary: Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves rules out a suggested Apple app-replacement mechanism for the foundation transfer, explaining that it covers successors from the same developer. The ownership-transfer opportunity remains in Building, with its separate migration plan still needed.

sources.title: Move companion app ownership to the foundation

roadmapUpdates.title: Feature discovery explores a shortcut in the server picker
roadmapUpdates.summary: Bruno Pantaleão Gonçalves adds a concrete idea to the Considering feature-discovery proposal: an entry in the server picker leading to location-based server-switching settings. It remains a design suggestion, without a rollout decision.
